newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs move higher but seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs move higher but seen rangebound.

text.p: Belgian bonds moved higher with Bunds in thin trading on Thursday, reversing the previous session's weakness and given a boost by Germany's March Ifo business climate index which was lower than forecast.
But with an absence of major U.S. ecnonimc data for the next few days plus a monthly auction coming up next Monday, OLOs were expected to remain range bound in the short term.

"There are no buyers because yields are too low and no sellers either," one dealer said. "Buyers will only be interested when the (10-year) yield gets up to 6.10 percent." By 0845 GMT the benchmark March 2007 OLO was yielding 5.95 percent.
This was just below Wednesday's close at 5.96 percent, and the spread over Germany remained steady at 12 basis points. Front month OLO futures climbed 27 bp to 120.66.
Dealers said there was so far little interest being expressed for the new January 2000 OLO to be auction on Monday. The current 10-year benchmark will also be on offer.
"People were interested in having a new five-year OLO at par because the current one is too expensive. But we could eventually see some switching into the new OLO from short term paper," one added.
